product: commentary — no product (a swipe-file promo for organic-looking ads)
hook: "organic looking ads are still the biggest cheat code in ecommerce" — the folder's namesake claim.
body: Argues organic-looking ads win because they don't feel like ads — they look like what a customer would already watch (dog getting brushed, messy demo, random phone clip, product used at home); no studio, no perfect lighting, no overproduced brand video; claims 200+ organic-looking ads from scaling brands (pets, beauty, skincare, supplements, weight loss).
cta: "rt + comment 'organic' and i'll send you the swipe file (must follow for dm)."
idea: The "cheat code" is nativity — a simple native-feeling visual that makes the product obvious beats studio production because the viewer's ad defenses never engage.
sequencing: The visual menu (dog brushed, messy demo, phone clip, at-home use)
The anti-list (no studio, no lighting, no brand video)
The proof (200+ ads from scaling brands)
formatting: Text post + 25s video; comment-gated lead magnet.
why_it_works: "Looks like something a customer would already watch" names the exact mechanism — pattern-matching to organic content bypasses banner blindness before the sell begins.
what_to_steal: LC's organic-looking lane: messy phone-clip jewelry demos (pool, shower, gym) with no studio lighting — the waterproof claim DEMANDS lo-fi proof.

product: commentary — no product (an AI-UGC tool pitch)
hook: "Ima Studio + Seedance 2.0 + GPT Image 2 = an absolute cheat code for beauty UGC ads." — tool-stack flex.
body: Pitches an AI beauty-UGC workflow: turns one lipstick image into realistic product demos, application close-ups, natural reactions, and polished final looks in minutes; contrasts with $150–$500 per real-UGC-creator video; scales variations across TikTok/IG/FB/Snap without new shoots.
cta: "Follow + RT + comment 'FACTORY' and I'll send you the step-by-step workflow and prompt. Must be following."
idea: The cheat code is AI-UGC unit economics — one product image becomes unlimited demo/close-up/reaction/final-look variations at near-zero marginal cost vs $150–$500 per human creator video.
sequencing: The stack (Ima Studio + Seedance 2.0 + GPT Image 2)
The cost contrast ($150–$500 per human video)
The output (demos, close-ups, reactions, final looks — in minutes)
The scale (4 platforms, no new shoots)
The ease claim ("anyone can create videos like this")
formatting: Text post + 18s video; tool-launch pitch with hashtags.
why_it_works: The $150–$500 anchor makes the AI workflow feel like found money — the entire pitch is cost-arbitrage, which is the language media buyers think in.
what_to_steal: The unit-economics framing for LC's AI-UGC program: one jewelry image → unlimited on-body demo variations; benchmark every AI asset against the $150–$500 human-creator cost.

product: commentary — no product (an SEO tactic post; off-topic for ad formats)
hook: "Investing in Google Ads is the ultimate SEO cheat code." — cross-channel arbitrage claim.
body: The tactic: use Google Ads conversion data to find the top-10 revenue keywords, then rank for them organically (optimize product/category pages + backlinks); case study: 4 months later the keywords hit #1, organic traffic and sales took off — "no better way to completely remove the guesswork from SEO."
idea: Paid search data de-risks SEO — buy the keyword intelligence with ads, then own the terms organically and stop paying per click.
sequencing: The play (rank for them, stop paying)
The case study (top-10 keywords → #1 in 4 months)
why_it_works: "Remove the guesswork" is the core appeal — it turns SEO from a gamble into an arbitrage with a known-ROI input.
what_to_steal: Nothing for LC's ad creative — but the paid-data-feeds-organic principle applies to LC's SEO: use Shopping/Search query data to pick jewelry SEO targets.

product: commentary — no product (a build-in-public dev diary; off-topic)
hook: "AquaVoice is a fucking cheat code." — tool hype.
body: Day-52 ecom diary: voice-dictated ad copy into Claude Code via AquaVoice after an Evolve podcast episode; 2 of 5 AI-written copies were launch-ready; expects fast format iteration; "hitting another meta ad spending limit" on the way to $100K/day.
idea: Voice-to-AI copy iteration is the cheat code — dictating into Claude Code produced launch-ready ad copy same-day, compressing the creative iteration loop.
why_it_works: Not applicable to ad formats — it's a workflow diary entry about AI-assisted copywriting speed.
what_to_steal: The workflow (voice-dictate hooks → Claude iterates → launch-ready copy same day) for LC's creative team — but that's ops, not a format.

product: commentary — no product (a competitive-intel tool pitch)
hook: "Trendtrack is a cheat code guys" — tool hype.
body: Pitches Trendtrack: Meta, TikTok, Google, emails, ads rank, EU ad spend, landing pages — "in one click, you have the entire e-com funnel of any shop or brand."
idea: Competitive funnel X-ray in one click — seeing any brand's full funnel (ads → LPs → emails) is the "cheat code" for creative research.
sequencing: The coverage (Meta, TikTok, Google, emails, ranks, spend, LPs)
The promise (any brand's entire funnel in one click)
The demo proof (55s video + 2 photos — the tool selling itself)
formatting: Text post + 55s video + 2 photos; tool demo.
why_it_works: "Entire e-com funnel in one click" sells the end of manual research — the cheat code is skipping the work, not doing it better.
what_to_steal: The research habit for LC: X-ray competitor jewelry funnels (ads → LPs → emails) before building LC's own variants — whatever tool does it.

product: commentary — no product (a founder-led ad workshop pitch)
hook: "absolute cheat code for any brand" — universal claim.
body: The cheat code has three parts: (1) native, viral format; (2) YOU are the best salesperson for your product; (3) pre-selected hooks fed through questions — mapped to differentiation, unique mechanism, objection handling, and launch teases; plus "hang with Josh" (event/workshop context).
idea: Founder-as-salesperson inside a native viral format, armed with pre-selected hooks delivered as Q&A — the founder's authenticity + a hook menu is the cheat code.
sequencing: The three parts (native format, founder = salesperson, pre-selected hooks)
why_it_works: "YOU are the best salesperson" flatters the founder-reader while the pre-selected-hooks mechanic removes the "what do I say" fear — it's a confidence product disguised as a tactic.
what_to_steal: LC's founder-led lane: Jay answering pre-selected hook questions on camera ("why doesn't it tarnish?", "why PVD over plating?") in native formats — founder authenticity + hook menu.

product: commentary — no product (a Claude-skills repo share; off-topic)
hook: "This is a f**king cheat code — Someone just published a skill pack with the skills used at Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and others" — insider-drop framing.
body: Shares ComposioHQ/awesome-claude-skills: SEO skills wired to Search Console/PageSpeed/Ads API, marketing (briefs, ad copy, LPs from one brand context file), finance, compliance, research, product — plus 30+ agents and 70+ commands; usage = clone repo, drop skill folder in, restart.
idea: Pre-built Claude skills are the cheat code — big-lab workflows (Anthropic/Google/OpenAI) packaged as drop-in skill folders.
sequencing: The skill menu (SEO, marketing, finance, compliance, research, product)
why_it_works: Not applicable to ad formats — it's a dev-tooling share that matched on "cheat code."
what_to_steal: The "one brand context file" idea for LC's AI creative pipeline — a single canon file (materials, warranty, voice) that every AI-generated asset draws from.

product: commentary — no product (a meta-rant about cheat-code culture itself)
hook: "Average beginner in ecom daily routine:" — satirical routine list.
body: Satirizes the beginner loop (check ROAS 0.9, blame Meta, doomscroll, bookmark another "secret cheat code for ecom," rip products on Kalo, post daily updates with no progress); argues guru "just run ads bro" advice sells courses, not results; the real skill: "Making ads that sell" — understanding why people buy, what hooks in 2 seconds, how to turn a cold stranger into a buyer.
idea: The cheat-code folder's own immune response — chasing "secret cheat codes" IS the beginner trap; the only real cheat code is the skill of making ads that sell.
sequencing: The satirical routine (wake → ROAS 0.9 → blame → doomscroll → bookmark cheat code → ...)
The diagnosis (guru business model = sell the map)
The costs ($5K burned, saturated product, no transferable learning)
The exception (lucky launchers exist, survivorship bias)
The skill definition (why people buy, 2-second hooks, stranger → buyer)
why_it_works: The routine list is painfully recognizable to its target reader — self-recognition creates the openness for the sermon that follows.
what_to_steal: The "skill over cheat codes" hiring/training bar for LC's creative team — hire people who understand why people buy, not people collecting swipe files.

hook: "There are 37 ad formats printing right now." — authority list promise.
body: 10 of 37 verified formats; longest runner was an AI podcast at 280 days; full doc linked with live ad + days active + brand ad count per format.
cta: Doc links ("No comment or follow needed").
idea: Format-list proof infrastructure — no cheat-code-specific content.
why_it_works: The days-active proof column, as established in prior folders.

product: commentary — no product (an Arcads tool pitch)
hook: "AI singing ads are killing it on Tiktok right now." — trend claim.
body: The "singing ads cheat code": pick a brand you love → make them a singing ad with Arcads (1 click from any script) → tag the brand → challenge a friend.
idea: The cheat code is a 4-step viral loop — brand pick → 1-click singing ad → brand tag → friend challenge — that turns an ad tool into a tagging/challenge mechanic.
sequencing: The trend claim (singing ads killing it)
The distribution mechanic (every made ad recruits its own audience via tag + challenge)
formatting: Short text post + 66s video; tool pitch.
why_it_works: The tag-a-brand + challenge-a-friend steps bake distribution into the creative act — every made ad recruits its own audience.
what_to_steal: The tag-and-challenge loop for LC's AI-song lane: fans make LC singing ads, tag @louisecarter, challenge a friend — UGC that distributes itself.

product: Albo (an organization/habits app — described in a breakdown of its viral slideshow ad)
hook: "This is wild 😭 4.3M views. 250K saves. On a 'weird habits' slideshow." — numbers-first disbelief.
body: Breaks down Albo's viral slideshow: aesthetic slides of "weird habits" that actually work — no product demo, no feature dump; the app is tucked in as one of the habits mid-slideshow; why it works (per the post): "weird habits" = curiosity not sales pitch, every slide feels like a tip from a friend, the app is habit #N not the hero, people saved an organization-app ad like a life hack; the steal-it recipe: 5–7 real screenshot-worthy tips, product as tip #4 or #5, app framed as a habit not a pitch.
idea: The Trojan-horse slideshow — lead with genuinely saveable tips, tuck the product in as one tip among many, and the ad gets saved like content instead of skipped like an ad.
sequencing: The anti-list (no demo, no feature dump)
The principle ("If they'd save the tips without the app, the format works")
formatting: Text post + 4 photos; ad-breakdown with a steal-it recipe (48 likes, 68 bookmarks).
why_it_works: "People saved an organization app ad like it was a life hack" — the save is the conversion; tucking the product mid-list lets the content earn the save before the pitch arrives.
what_to_steal: LC's "7 waterproof-life hacks" slideshow: 6 genuinely useful tips (how to layer, how to clean, travel packing) with an LC piece tucked in as hack #4 — "if they'd save the tips without the jewelry, the format works."

hook: "if you're running paid ads to a b2c or b2b offer, post clips" — direct imperative.
body: The billboard analogy: clips are like billboards — you drive past, think nothing of it, but later your brain links a skippable ad back to the brand you saw on a billboard 2 weeks ago (familiarity); so: post clips, get millions of views, run retargeting, get "INSANELY cheap CACs" — "it's a cheat code lol."
idea: Organic clips are familiarity infrastructure — they pre-wire brand recognition so that later paid ads get watched instead of skipped, collapsing CAC.
sequencing: The payoff (millions of views → retargeting → insanely cheap CACs)
The shrug ("it's a cheat code lol")
why_it_works: The mere-exposure effect, explained through a billboard everyone has experienced — familiarity is the cheapest conversion asset there is.
what_to_steal: LC's organic clip engine feeding paid retargeting: viral jewelry clips build the familiarity pool; retargeting harvests it at collapsed CACs.

hook: "Something I've learned recently that will help if you're struggling with coming up with high converting concepts" — peer-help framing.
body: The tip: when ideating UGC concepts/scripts, read the comment sections on top-performing TikTok/Meta ads — real customers state their struggles in their own language; take ONE comment and build an ad concept around that customer language; the poster reports "huge improvement" in concepts since doing this — "Basing concepts off of real customer language is literally a script writing cheat code."
idea: Comment sections are free voice-of-customer research — one real customer comment, in their own words, is a complete ad concept.
sequencing: The method (read comments on top ads)
The insight (customers state struggles in their own language)
formatting: Short text post; UGC-community style with hashtags.
why_it_works: Customer language carries built-in resonance — a concept built from a real comment arrives pre-validated by the exact words the audience uses.
what_to_steal: LC's concept pipeline: mine comments on LC's top ads + competitor jewelry ads for customer language ("turns my neck green," "can't shower with it") — one comment = one UGC concept.
